newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech M2 figures give Cbank room, but no move seen.
newsitem.headline: Czech M2 figures give Cbank room, but no move seen.

text.p: A continued slowing in growth of the Czech money supply in February has given the central bank room to lower interest rates, analysts said on Monday, but the central bank ruled out any such move.
The Czech National Bank (CNB) said growth of its key money supply measure, M2, in February was 6.2 percent, year-on-year, down from 18.3 percent for the same month in 1996.

"The development of money supply in February confirms that lowering the minimum reserve requiremement to the level of 9.5 percent (from 11.5 percent), effective May 8,...was justified and adequate to the situation," central bank press spokesman Martin Svehla told Reuters.
Asked whether the figures meant the central bank was not planing any monetary policy changes in the near future Svehla said: "No, they are not being prepared," he said.
Most analysts said Svehla's comments were not surprising given the central bank has repeatedly said it was not considering any further changes to its current monetary policy.
But some said they were puzzled by the CNB's line of thinking, given it has said strong M2 growth is one of the main reasons behind its policies.

"The central bank has said in the first two months that M2 was the reason for high interest rates, and now it has gone below (the CNB's) target range," said Matt Starr, head of Capital Markets at Creditantstalt in Prague.
"We have no idea why this (data) does not call for a reversal of the trend. At this point, I have no idea what the CNB's objectives are," he added.
Last summer the CNB implemented a series of tightening moves, including a raising of its key discount rate by one percentage point to 10.5 percent.

Some analysts said they thought the central bank may now wait until June before acting, giving it time to assess the impact on the economy of a package of measures introduced by the government last week to cut internal and external deficits and spur growth.
In announcing the package, the government also called for monetary policy to be less restrictive, and has been critical of the policies saying economic growth is being sacrificed.
"We think there may be a slight cut in the repo rate soon, but I doubt there will be little more from the central bank at this point," said one foreign exchange dealer.
The Czech crown strengthened slightly after the M2 figures, rising about 10 basis points against its dollar/mark basket midpoint to 2.60 on the depreciation side of parity.
Earlier on Monday, the central bank fixed the crown at 2.69 percent on the depreciation side of parity.
